title: Evaluation of internal Hom on an affine open is bijective
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $\mathcal F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module. For every affine open $U\subset X$, the map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal M,\mathcal F))\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal M(U),\mathcal F(U))$ sending a morphism on the opens over $U$ to its component at $U$ is bijective. Internal Hom is the sheaf in [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. No quasi-coherence or finite-presentation hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01I7, lemma-compare-constructions; duality.tex Tag 0BUZ, sections clause

proof.text: Restrict M,F to U and identify U with Spec R for R=Gamma(U,O). The internal Hom over U is the morphisms between these restrictions, by its definition. Quasi-coherence is preserved by restriction and identifies M|U with the tilde of M(U), compatibly with sections, using the invertible tilde/global-sections counit.

Apply the tilde/global-sections adjunction to tilde(M(U)) and F|U. It is valid for arbitrary F. Under the unit isomorphism the Hom bijection is the component on sections at U. Precomposition with the counit and the chart identifications therefore make precisely the stated evaluation map bijective. For the empty open all the modules are zero.
